newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares tumble amid pre-holiday jitters.
newsitem.headline: German shares tumble amid pre-holiday jitters.

text.p: German shares peaked and troughed over the course of electronic trade on Wednesday, hitting record highs before tumbling to end over one percent lower after a jittery session before a German regional holiday.

The German equity market became even more paranoid after the French stock market dropped four percent on rumours that polls showed the opposition Socialists were well placed for Sunday's run-off parliamentary elections.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended down 38.83 points, or 1.06 percent, at 3,626.60 points.
Its bourse counterpart, the DAX index, ended down 37.94 points, or 1.03 percent, at 3,536.42 points.
Many market players were unwilling to take new positions ahead of Corpus Christi, which is a market and public holiday in southern German states.

"The weakness today is mostly due to the Corpus Christi regional holiday tomorrow, because a lot of people will take Friday off and turn it into a long weekend. Also everyone is nervous ahead of the French elections," a trader said.
The markets would read a victory for the left in France as negative for EMU stability, the trader said.
Among the main features on the market was Daimler-Benz AG, which forecast a rise in sales and earnings in full-year 1997, while sales in the first four months rose 15 percent to 36.3 million marks.
The shares rose to a high of 136.45 marks early on, but despite the upbeat figures, ended the day down 2.20 marks at 133.90 marks.
"It is increasingly the case that it is better to travel than arrive with the stock market the way it is at the moment," a trader said.
"The Daimler figures were in line, but everyone is looking for something special, a little bit extra, in the current climate," he said.
Another big mover over the day was carmaker BMW which ended down nearly four percent at 1,428 marks, having earlier gone as high as 1,510 marks.
Dealers said that the stock has become quite volatile of late, and that today's performance bore out that view.

Insurance giant Allianz AG Holding also ended lower. Shares rose over 1.20 percent to 385.50 marks, but fell over the day and ended down 63.50 marks at 375.50 marks, which traders said was due to profit-taking.
